resources.string: Slower intervals can show higher latency, because Wi-Fi power saving may put the radio to sleep between pings.

Asks Android to keep Wi-Fi out of power saving during the test. On Android 10 and newer it only works while the screen is on and NetPulse is in the foreground, and it uses a little more battery. Results then show best-case latency.
Measures how fast DNS servers answer real queries. This is separate from ping.
Asks for a popular name the server has already stored, so it shows the fastest possible answer.

Asks for a random name nobody has requested, so the server must look it up first. The answer is usually NXDOMAIN (name does not exist), which is still a real response, and it shows a typical fresh lookup.
Each server gets a short warm-up first, then queries are sent every 0.2 s. Warm-up results are not counted.
Queries for example.com (and random names under it) go directly to each server listed below. Nothing else is sent.
